notes:
Summary: Mid-market analytics SaaS (product analytics dashboards) evaluating Redwood after 4-week Hosted API trial. Primary goal: move latency-sensitive in-app assistant and on-demand report summarization from Hosted to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost ceilings.

PoC findings: hosted trial was positive for feature accuracy but highlighted two operational needs: (1) peak concurrency on release days causes 95/99 pct latency spikes, (2) a non-trivial share of tokens are long-form outputs (summaries ~800-2,500 tokens).

Workload profile (from trial logs): average QPS low (~1.8 qps), but peak QPS 10-14 qps during product release windows (5–15 minute bursts). Concurrency: median concurrency 2, 95th percentile concurrency ~9, observed short windows hitting ~16 concurrent streams. Token mix estimate: ~60% short prompts/responses (<=128 tokens), ~20% medium (129-1024), ~20% long summaries (800-2500).

Requirements: 90–95th pct latency target <200ms for short prompts; cost sensitivity moderate — finance wants predictability (commit + burstable). Must support SSO (SAML), KMS for key management, audit logs retention 1 year, and VPC peering for data egress rules. Data residency: EU customers only for some accounts — will need region pinning for subset.

- SE to deliver Dedicated capacity spreadsheet (GPU types, expected concurrency per replica, batching config, prefix cache benefit estimate) — due 2025-02-20.
- AE to propose contract sketch with 12-month reserved capacity + burst pool pricing.
- Finance to review projected ARR vs. cost model (drive doc shared).
- Legal to review data residency clause (POC ticket SEC-2143).
